title: Afghanistan: 5 Years in the Dark
gist: A first-person account of a 24-year-old former medical student, Fatima, in Kabul describes how the Taliban's five-year rule has erased the Afghanistan that once had a constitution, a free press, and women in universities and courtrooms.

themes.theme: Personal testimony of lost freedoms under Taliban rule

insights.claim: A 24-year-old woman named Fatima, once a university student intending to become a doctor, now describes herself as a prisoner in her own home in Kabul under Taliban rule.
insights.speaker: Nasratullah Taban
insights.so_what: Individual testimony documents the human capital loss under Taliban restrictions on women, relevant context for humanitarian, aid, and ESG-linked assessments of Afghanistan and the region.
insights.quote: Sometimes I look at a bird and feel jealous, because it has more freedom than I do

insights.claim: The Afghanistan that existed before the Taliban's 2021 return had a constitution, a free press, and women present in universities, courtrooms, and newsrooms; the author states that state no longer exists.
insights.speaker: Nasratullah Taban
insights.so_what: A stark before/after framing of institutional collapse (constitution, press freedom, women's participation) underscores the scale of governance and civil-society reversal in Afghanistan since 2021.
insights.quote: The Afghanistan that printed the card – a state with a constitution, a free press and women in its universities, courtrooms, and newsrooms – no longer exists.
insights.locator: The Afghanistan that printed the card
